chase_cards.name: Unown J [Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 8]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is not loud by price or trophy aura; it is a little alphabet hinge. J reaches collectors through a specialist magazine insert, then asks to be read with O, I, and N as a word inside the play system.

key_artists.name: Hideki Kazama
key_artists.why: Kazama matters here because Unown is design reduced to almost pure sign. The card is creature, letter, and rule object at once, and the illustrator credit helps keep that graphic identity attached to the exact magazine promo route.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 8 insert source group as one row containing Unown J at source index 208.
Bulbapedia places the Japanese Unown J print in Unnumbered Promotional cards and identifies its release as a Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 8 insert on September 1, 2000.
Bulbapedia identifies Unown J as a Psychic-type Basic Pokémon card with 30 HP and the Hidden Power attack.
Bulbapedia says Unown J's Pokémon Power applies only if Unown J, Unown O, Unown I, and Unown N are on the player's Bench.
Bulbapedia credits the Unown J artwork to Hideki Kazama.
Bulbapedia's Hideki Kazama category includes multiple Unown letter cards, tying Kazama's early TCG credit surface to the alphabet-creature lane.
Bulbapedia says the English version of Unown J was released as Wizards Black Star Promo 38 and was available with Spell of the Unown: Entei on VHS or DVD.

Bulbapedia says the Generation II Unown forms J and R were not released in a Japanese or English expansion; they were instead released as Japanese Unnumbered Promotional cards and English Wizards Black Star Promos.
As judged collector texture, Unown J matters because it turns the alphabet into both distribution puzzle and play puzzle: a single magazine insert that also points sideways to O, I, and N.

narrative.human_title: Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 8 Unown J: a letter that wants company
narrative.why_it_matters: Unown J is one of those small cards that explains why a collector catalog needs more than names and dates. It arrived through Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 8, not a booster pack, and it is built like a tiny instruction to look sideways: J only fully wakes up beside O, I, and N. The card is a letter, a creature, a magazine insert, a Kazama graphic object, and a missing Neo-expansion edge case all at once.

narrative.human_title: Unown J: the letter that needs O, I, and N
narrative.why_it_matters: Unown J is wonderfully literal. It is a letter Pokémon, a magazine insert, and a card whose own rules ask it to assemble a word with its neighbors. That makes it a perfect agent-catalog card: the name is not enough, the letter is not enough, the artwork is not enough. You need the Trainers Vol. 8 route, the Japanese unnumbered promo identity, and the J/O/I/N context before the object really comes into focus.
